1.explanation: To implement a secondary style for Tabs you need to update both the overall Tabs container and the individual Tab and TabContent elements. The Tabs files define the container logic and root styles; the Tab files control each tab’s typography, padding, and active/inactive states; the TabContent files handle the content area styling. Together these six documents are where you’d add class names or Sass variables and write the CSS rules needed to reproduce the requested design.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshot shows the Tabs component rendered with a new “secondary” look: two adjacent tabs (“Application Discovery” and “Enterprise Artifacts”) on a light gray background. The active tab (“Application Discovery”) has blue text and a colored bottom border, while the inactive tab is rendered in muted text with no highlight. This variant deviates from the default Carbon Tabs styling and needs a new style class or token.
